---
title: "Assigning building components"
lang: en
---
Component assignment connects geometry, quantities and life-cycle assessment. **A geometric area alone is not a complete LCA assignment.** Construction, boundary condition and use must be traceable.

[![Component types: assignment in the building section](../media/components.png){.full-figure}](../media/components.png)

The original diagram adds cases beyond the simplified schematic sections. Click to enlarge. Source: `docs/ComponentTypes.png`; see also [training slides 13–14](../downloads/schulung.pdf).

## Project workflow

1. Assign areas and components from the actual construction design.
2. Distinguish external air, ground, heated spaces and unheated adjacent spaces.
3. Check quantities and units before importing LCA factors.
4. Document elements that are not shown separately, such as balconies, columns or window frames.
5. Review assigned component values and the assessment boundary.

<details><summary>Technical interpretation</summary>In the second reference model, the basement ceiling separates heated from unheated space and forms part of the thermal boundary. The internal floor slab is also a construction component included in the balance, but it is not an external thermal boundary there. Thermal and life-cycle balances describe different properties of the same component.</details>

**Further reading:** [Importing LCA data](climate.qmd#eco2soft) · [Assessing embodied emissions](climate.qmd).

## Assignment in the Excel tool {#excel-assignment}

**Thermal inputs:** [🧱 Bauphysik]{.excel-menu .darkred} worksheet → opaque and transparent components.

**Life-cycle assessment:** [☁ Treibhauspotential (THG)]{.excel-menu .teal} worksheet → [Baulich]{.excel-section}.

::: {.excel-operation}
Assign category, construction and quantity for external walls, windows, roofs, basement ceilings/foundations and intermediate floors. Check that additional building measures, grouped measures and a total LCA entry do not overlap. A component that is not needed to define the thermal envelope may still contribute to embodied emissions.
:::

[Life-cycle assessment and Eco2soft](climate.qmd#eco2soft)

## From section to category

The second schematic section has two heated storeys and an explicitly **unheated basement**. The selector switches between categories. The list also names categories absent from this geometry; do not reinterpret them as other components.
